problem: The bullet says that if you take I2 as pointing out of port 2, then B and D change sign. That is false. The parameters A, B, C, D are properties of the network and do not depend on which way you draw I2. If you draw I2 leaving port 2 and write [V1; I1] = [[A, B], [C, D]][V2; I2], the numbers for B and D stay the same as in the chapter; only the sign inside the equation changes. B and D flip sign only if you keep I2 as entering port 2 but drop the minus sign, i.e. write [V1; I1] = [[A, B], [C, D]][V2; I2]. As written, a student will wrongly believe the measured B and D values change when the arrow on I2 is reversed.
fix: The minus sign on I2 is part of the convention. If you keep I2 as entering port 2 but drop the minus sign and write [V1; I1] = [[A, B], [C, D]][V2; I2], then B and D change sign. Drawing I2 as leaving port 2 and writing the equation with +I2 leaves the values of A, B, C, D unchanged.
